items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: And, Bud, I knew in St. Louis, his brother lives here in town.

ctx.x: Well Joe Clancy is famous, the stories about him. Yeah. Francis Murray, who you probably don't remember, he was a young man, and a saxophone player where he used to play stories about Joe Clancy. Well anyway, was there any special sort of ligature you used to, or that people generally use since you worked in the store?

Ligatures, most all of them are made in France, and there are different names put on them. The banal, the O-N-A-B-E, is what I actually used. But there are so many different variations of them. I just recently sent one that I got to put Brown in the water. And, Bud, I knew in St. Louis, his brother lives here in town. And he, I had this patented special ligature made by Gigliotti, he's a famous plant editor, and it was good, but I didn't find a big picture of the difference. It was made of plastic, and I had a…
I've even seen people pass string around there. Were you to believe in that?
